claims.statement: In the Episode 16 OhMyGame-managed Web session, the Castellan's 3.8-second first Rupture was not reliably captured: the Web game load varied from about 5 to 30 seconds, fixed waits missed the cast, and the scenario exposed no ready event or paused opening.

attributes.scope: One app-managed Godot Web investigation of the Atlas Castellan opening in Episode 16.
attributes.original_outcome: The managed loop reached the scenario, but the first 1.8-second cast and its 4-second interrupt were not captured.
attributes.revisit_when: When a ready signal, held opening or paused cast makes the first decision observable through the managed runtime.
attributes.claim_ceiling: One project, one session and one timing window; the load-time range is observed, not a general Web-load benchmark.

claims.statement: In Episode 17, a project-owned ready hold, a pause at the first Rupture and F10 reset made the real Castellan cast observable and repeatable through OhMyGame's managed Web runtime; A interrupted from the held cast for the real 4-second window, B accepted the Rupture and earned the 2-second outside-cast recovery, and C reached the later cast with the 60% cover notch, which completed without companion cover.

attributes.scope: One app-managed Web encounter, three controlled investigations and two source revisions.
attributes.original_outcome: The first cast interrupt, accepted-cast recovery and later-cast cover notch became observable; the later 2-second cancel did not resolve.
attributes.revisit_when: When a natural-speed or human run measures answerability, readability or cover under the unheld window.
attributes.claim_ceiling: A/B used a6ddcb8 and C used dd91a5c; both sourceDirty=false. A and B held the cast; C used a support party. No human qualification or natural-route evidence.

claims.statement: An interaction that resolves faster than the investigator's end-to-end observe-reason-act cycle, including build, load, capture and tool latency, cannot be reliably investigated from an uncontrolled real-time run; the development environment needs an explicit, reversible temporal control that reaches and holds the interaction without changing its rules. Where the hold is placed determines what it preserves: a hold before the action can preserve execution timing while extending decision time; a hold during the action preserves neither. The controlled observation establishes the interaction's presentation, rules and consequences, not natural-speed answerability, readability, player experience or natural-route frequency.

attributes.scope: Development-environment design for investigating transient, time-bounded gameplay interactions, especially agent-driven or tool-mediated playtesting of combat, narrative or UI states that resolve faster than the investigator can observe and act.
conditions: The question depends on observing a transient rendered state or its resolution, not only an event log or deterministic contract.
The investigator's cycle exceeds the interaction window, or the window's timing is otherwise uncontrollable.

A development-only control can hold the state without changing the interaction's rules, cooldowns, damage, AI or companion behavior; the held state is reachable on the natural route, and entry into the hold is verified against an unheld run.
The control is selectable, so the same scenario can produce held and unheld observations; the control, its placement and the build identity are recorded.
A readiness signal or deterministic entry point replaces fixed waits.
The control does not reveal hidden state the player could not see, when the question is about player-readable information.
attributes.counterevidence: A mechanical-contract question is adequately answered by telemetry or a deterministic probe; a hold adds fidelity cost without benefit. When the interaction's meaning is its time pressure (parry, multiplayer, horror), a hold removes the phenomenon and can show the rule but not the experience. A technically unfaithful hold (network, timers, animation, party pressure) can create a state the game cannot produce. When the natural route already reaches the interaction reliably, the hold may be unnecessary and may introduce lab artifacts. An intentionally rare interaction is not a defect; a controlled scenario is the right tool, not a design change.
attributes.revisit_when: A human or natural-speed run measures readability or answerability under the real window; the harness supports deterministic replay or event-level inspection without pausing; or a held and an unheld investigation of the same interaction disagree.
attributes.claim_ceiling: One encounter, one engine and three controlled investigations (A/B/C); no human play; A/B and C used different source revisions and parties; the hold's effect on readability and feasibility was not measured; the later 60% cover was observed but did not resolve.
